mbm-1101.clue: I leave a little clay on the saucer.
mbm-1101.quote: The tiny clay snail I made as a handle slid off my mug during firing and stuck to the saucer instead. I’ve been setting the cup down beside him very carefully ever since.

mbm-1102.clue: It fits inside my pencil case.
mbm-1102.quote: I fold an old pocket timetable around my pencils on drawing days at the station. The worn fold opens straight to my first solo trip, a local with six stops and one extraordinary viaduct.

mbm-1103.clue: Our club has three different moons.
mbm-1103.quote: We drew the final rooftop scene from memory after our anime tape ended. I drew a crescent, two friends drew full moons, and the fourth drew a streetlight. Only the streetlight was actually in the film.

mbm-1104.clue: I saved the orange peel from my first meet.
mbm-1104.quote: My coach gave me an orange between lifting sets and peeled the skin in one long spiral. I drew it in my log above the weight I’d just lifted. Now every good day gets a tiny orange curl.

mbm-1105.clue: I watched the lily drift upriver.
mbm-1105.quote: A lily petal circled my kayak in a little eddy, then sailed upstream for a moment. I stopped paddling and let it show me a patch of the creek I’d never noticed.

mbm-1106.clue: My smallest tool sleeps in leather.
mbm-1106.quote: My sister’s sewing scissors have points sharp enough to poke through her bag. I cut a leather sheath shaped like a honeybee. The handles stick out behind it like two round wings.

mbm-1107.clue: I found another sky beneath the reeds.
mbm-1107.quote: I paddled out before the wind picked up and the water held the whole morning sky. A single falling seed made ripples big enough to bend a cloud. I stayed to watch it straighten.

mbm-1108.clue: I can read a whole chapter through one stripe.
mbm-1108.quote: My beach umbrella has a translucent orange stripe. Late in the afternoon it turns my paperback pages the color of honey. That’s when I fold the corner and go for lemonade.

mbm-1109.clue: I put a bell on the bird feeder once.
mbm-1109.quote: I hoped I could hear a bird land. The first visitor was so light the bell stayed quiet. I took it off and learned to wait by the window with my sketchbook open instead.

mbm-1110.clue: That little cork pawn has a tall hat.
mbm-1110.quote: We lost a pawn at the park so the groundskeeper carved one from a cork. His pocketknife left a point on top. I let the tall fellow lead off every game I play on that board.

mbm-1111.clue: I give the last player a parade.
mbm-1111.quote: At the end of our board game I line up all the wooden pieces along the final stretch. My little cousin likes bringing up the rear because his green wagon gets the whole parade.

mbm-1112.clue: I keep the pattern beside my coffee.
mbm-1112.quote: My grandmother traced a spray of leaves for the side of my cousin’s pollera. I stitched one leaf in a lighter green. Whenever she turns, that pale one catches the sunlight first.

mbm-1113.clue: I asked for one tiny spoon.
mbm-1113.quote: The pudding contest put a huge spoon beside every bowl. I borrowed my niece’s little silver one and ate at my own pace. My ribbon still smells faintly of butterscotch.

mbm-1114.clue: I gave the quilt a pocket watch.
mbm-1114.quote: Granddad’s old watch stopped one winter. I stitched a little clock face from its outline and tucked the real watch into the pocket behind it. He likes having both kinds of time close at hand.

mbm-1115.clue: I guessed the ending from the couch.
mbm-1115.quote: Our pajamas-and-movie club hands out a paper crown for guessing the twist. I wore mine during the next film and its points cast a second crown just above the villain’s head.

mbm-1116.clue: I made a woolly cactus for a thirsty window.
mbm-1116.quote: The kitchen windowsill gets so hot I crochet plants for it. My green cactus has a red flower and a bent little arm. I keep a thimble beside it as a very unnecessary watering can.

mbm-1117.clue: I stitched the puddles in silver.
mbm-1117.quote: My quilt follows our walk home in the rain. Every puddle is a little oval of silver cloth from a costume jacket. My nephew leaps his fingers across them in his socks.

mbm-1118.clue: I hear the opening note from the lobby.
mbm-1118.quote: The DJ at our favorite club plays one high piano note before our song. I heard it from the coat counter and came running with my scarf still trailing. My friends held a spot in the circle.

mbm-1119.quote: After the peach-pie contest the organizer takes one picture of everybody’s faces. Mine always has a neat streak along one eyebrow, no matter how carefully I eat. My aunt keeps them in date order.

mbm-1120.clue: I make one square with the lights off.
mbm-1120.quote: My quilting friend reads textures with her fingertips. We picked velvet, corduroy and smooth cotton in the dark and made her a patchwork star. She knew which corner was mine without looking.

mbm-1121.clue: I sew the border after breakfast.
mbm-1121.quote: My cousin’s quilt has a border of little fried eggs cut from yellow and white scraps. One egg has two yolks. That’s the one he pats after a good morning at school.

mbm-1122.clue: I started the tune on an empty bus.
mbm-1122.quote: The accordion case rested on my knees while I tapped out a vallenato rhythm on its latches. At the next stop a passenger picked up the beat with her keys. We rode three stops together.

mbm-1123.clue: My Thursday sewing circle takes one subway token.
mbm-1123.quote: The tile under my quilting frame has a dip. I slid my last old subway token under one leg to steady it. Every Thursday I pay the same fare and spend the whole evening in my front room.

mbm-1124.clue: I keep the hat upside down at breakfast.
mbm-1124.quote: I practice making a paper rose appear from my hat while the kettle warms. Mum left a real rose inside it one morning. I’ve never had a volunteer improve a trick quite that much.

mbm-1125.quote: My flying notebook records my first solo and my first smooth crosswind landing. There’s also a drawing of my first sandwich eaten under the wing while waiting out the rain. That one tasted like a medal.
